findings.description: Host-order fidelity is supplied by the DispatchProxy ILibraryManager double (HostOrderedLibraryManager: SortName Ordinal ASC then raw Name Ordinal ASC), not by the pinned Jellyfin SQL query. It cannot reproduce host collation, SortName normalization, nullable SortName, or the unspecified tie-break; the fixtures are ASCII and the behavior under test (locate-by-itemId, strict-after, N+QueueCapacity bound) is host-collation-independent, so this is a registered substitute, not a false-confidence path. The worker report records it in known_limitations (it does not run the host SQL), and the live-host verifier / task 19.5 own the host-order residual (F4-R4).

findings.description: Requirement 2's 'became ineligible' anchor is exercised as an item leaving the Movie/Episode candidate enumeration (a Movie retyped as a Series), not as a Movie/Episode that remains enumerable but becomes service-ineligible (remote location, no match). The worker documents this interpretation: an item that stays a candidate is still located by identity, so the cursor correctly does not reset. The enumerated-but-ineligible path is separately exercised by the existing 19.1 fact AnItemThatNeedsNoWorkIsCoveredAndDoesNotStallTheCursor, so the suite does not leave the distinction untested; only the wording of the new file's scenario label could invite a broader reading.

findings.description: For the post-save path, the literal requirement 'does not read ... the cursor' is established only by observable effects: no locate walk (Requests == [(0,2),(2,2)]) and a byte-identical cursor record. A hypothetical non-authoritative cursor read that did not affect enumeration would leave both assertions green. The reflection fact's absence check enumerates the per-item/trigger types, not the internal source branch of LibraryReconciliationService (which legitimately holds the store). The runtime consequence (no resume) is caught (mutation probe E, independently reproduced: PostSave made cursor-governed fails AcceptedItems).

findings.description: The webhook trigger-exclusion fact is the only wall-clock-dependent case. It uses a bounded condition poll (500 attempts x 10 ms, ~5 s maximum) and then asserts the condition was observed, so it can neither pass vacuously nor hang indefinitely; the other 18 cases are synchronous. Worker report documents this. Verified: WaitUntilAsync returns condition() after the loop and the caller asserts Assert.True, and the harness/loop cancels on StopAsync. No fixed sleep and no assertion depends on elapsed time.
evidence: Matrix filter ran 5 consecutive times: Passed 19/19 each run (no observed flake)

findings.description: Verification requirement 11 lists 'yields per clause 7'; the suite asserts the batch/page bound, every page request == ReconciliationBatchSize, and cancellation inside and between pages, but does not (and structurally cannot, from a black-box test) assert the Task.Yield between pages. The yield is not externally observable behavior and the bounded-page assertions are the load-bearing part of the requirement.

summary: The 19.2 matrix is a genuine integration of the real JellyfinMediaLibraryEnumerator, the real LibraryReconciliationService, a real ReconciliationCursorStore over a temporary StateRepository, and the real LibraryWorkQueue; only ILibraryManager (and unused coordinator/metadata boundaries) are doubled, which is identified and registered rather than hidden. All 12 verification_requirements_for_19_2 cases map to facts that fail under the specific defect they claim to detect. I independently reproduced all ten mutation probes (A-J) in a scratch copy outside the repository: A (page-aligned resume), B (Coalesced treated as a stop), C (overflowed/stopped item counted covered), D (scope check bypassed), E (PostSave cursor-governed), F (Stopped clause removed), G (resume offset ignored), H (unlocatable anchor reported located), I (InFlight treated as a stop), and J (cursor always wrapped) each failed exactly the claimed fact(s), with the worker's expected/actual messages matched where reported. Requirements 3, 4, 7, 9, 10 and the N-dependent page-reach bound are asserted with load-bearing (not tautological) assertions; the tie residual is exercised honestly as a deferral and never asserted as covered, and the page-reach bound is asserted as N + QueueCapacity and demonstrably sensitive (probe G read 14 rows for N=8 > 11). No test is skipped on this task's account; the default suite reproduces Failed 0 / Passed 1873 / Skipped 64 / Total 1937 (+19 passed, +19 total, 0 new skips). No production code was changed. Findings are LOW/INFORMATIONAL only (host-order substitute, ineligibility wording, the literal post-save read-exclusion, the single bounded async poll, and the unobservable Task.Yield); none undermines confidence in the shipped behavior. No BLOCKER or HIGH remains, so the matrix is approved with minor findings.
